jobs.occupation: PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water

Research area and project description:
Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts wet biogenic residues such as manure, biogas digestate and organic household waste into a renewable biocrude that can be upgraded to marine and aviation fuels. Alongside the biocrude, HTL produces large volumes of process water rich in dissolved organics and nitrogen. Treating this water efficiently while recovering its energy and nutrients is essential for the sustainability and economics of future full-scale HTL plants.

The PhD position is part of the Horizon Europe Innovation Action CARAVEL (2027-2030), coordinated by Aarhus University with 16 partners from 8 countries. CARAVEL will demonstrate the first integrated HTL value chain at TRL8, including circular management of process water and hydrochar. It is a collaborative project, so frequent exchange with the international partners from academia and industry is essential.

The PhD project will investigate anaerobic digestion (AD) as a route to convert HTL process water into biogas while managing nitrogen. HTL process water contains compounds such as phenols and N-heterocycles that can inhibit methanogenesis, and inhibition thresholds depend on feedstock and process conditions. The PhD student will determine biomethane potential and inhibitory effects of process waters from different feedstocks in batch co-digestion tests with manure, demonstrate co-digestion in a full-scale experimental thermophilic biogas reactor, and optimise mono-digestion in a pilot-scale anaerobic fixed-bed biofilter, including micro-aeration to enhance the degradation of inhibitory compounds. A central aim is to link process water composition to methane yield, process stability and nitrogen conversion.

The work combines laboratory experiments with pilot- and full-scale operation at AU Foulum, which hosts both HTL and biogas research facilities. Techniques include biomethane potential testing, reactor operation, gas analysis, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis, and GC-MS characterisation of process water.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants must have a relevant Master's degree, e.g. in environmental, chemical or biological engineering, biotechnology, microbiology or a similar field.

Experience with anaerobic digestion, biogas processes or wastewater treatment is expected. Practical experience with laboratory or pilot-scale bioreactor operation and relevant analytical techniques (e.g. gas chromatography, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis) is desired. Knowledge of hydrothermal liquefaction or other thermochemical conversion technologies is an advantage but not a requirement.

The successful candidate has demonstrated excellent academic results, has good collaboration and communication skills in English and is also able to work independently.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Burrehøjvej 43, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Library and Digital Media Officer

Job Type: Part-time (with possibility of full-time conversion) | Workplace: Copenhagen, Denmark | Employer: China Cultural Center in Copenhagen

 

About the Organization

The China Cultural Center in Copenhagen is an official institution dedicated to promoting cultural and tourism exchanges between China and Denmark at both governmental and grassroots levels. We organize cultural events, facilitate people-to-people exchanges, and collaborate with Danish institutions and travel trade partners to enhance mutual understanding and cooperation.

We are currently seeking a motivated and experienced professional to join our team and to serve as an important communication window for promoting Chinese culture to Danish and international audiences.

 

Job Description

The Library and Digital Media Officer is responsible for the management and operation of the China Cultural Center's digital media platforms and library, as well as the promotion of the Center's cultural activities and public services.

 

Key Responsibilities

 ⑴ Social Media Management and Digital Communications

Manage and maintain the Center's social media accounts and digital platforms, including WeChat Official Account, Facebook, Instagram and the Center's official website. 

Plan, create, edit and publish communication materials, including news articles, event announcements, promotional posts, photographs, videos and other digital content.

Develop and implement social media content plans in accordance with the Center's events and communication objectives.

Monitor platform performance, analyse engagement and audience data, and continuously improve content quality and online visibility.

Coordinate photography, video recording, editing and the archiving of promotional materials for the Center's activities.

 ⑵ Library Management and Public Services

Oversee the daily operations of the Center's library, including book classification, cataloguing, registration, lending, returns and collection management.

Establish and maintain library management procedures and reader services, including opening arrangements, reservations and visitor reception.

Actively promote the opening of the library to the general public and expand its readership among local residents and communities.

Plan and organise reading promotion activities, book-sharing sessions, cultural talks and other public cultural activities.

Promote the library's resources and services to increase its visibility and accessibility within the local community.

⑶ Cultural Communications and General Support

Support the promotion and publicity of the Center's cultural events, exhibitions, performances, lectures and cultural exchange activities.

Photograph cultural events and create visual content for the Center's promotional and communication purposes.

Participate in developing communication strategies, preparing promotional materials, writing copy and producing multimedia content.

Assist in establishing and maintaining relationships with local communities, schools, cultural institutions and other relevant organisations to expand partnerships and promote public cultural services.

Undertake other related duties as assigned by the Center.

 

Essential:

1. Language: Fluent proficiency in both Chinese and English (written and spoken).

2. Industry Knowledge: Professional knowledge of social media management and digital platform operations. Proficiency in using standard office software and applications.

3. Paper Work Ability: written communication and analytical reporting skills.

4. Education: Bachelor's degree or above.

5. Background Check: An acceptable criminal record check is required and Applicants must have the legal right to work in Denmark.

6. Health: Ability to provide a health certificate as required by the employer.

 

Preferred:

1. Proficiency in Danish is a strong advantage.

 

Work Authorization

During the interview stage, candidates will be asked to confirm their current residence status in Denmark. For positions involving international travel, verification of legal work authorization may be required prior to final offer.

 

Selection Process & Interview

To apply for this position, please submit the following to our email:

① Your CV/resume;

② A written proposal outlining how you would develop and manage the media and digital communication platforms of the China Cultural Center in Copenhagen.

 (format: Word or PDF)

 

Selection Timeline:

1. Applications will be screened on a rolling basis, and shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

2. If you have not received an email response by 31 December, 2026, please assume that your application has not been shortlisted for an interview.

 

Special Terms of Employment

This position starts on a part-time basis. The Center may offer a one-year full-time contract, based on work performance and business needs. The final interpretation of these employment terms shall reside with the Center.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professors in AI Engineering
jobs.description:
SDU Centre for Industrial Software in Sønderborg, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within AI Engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates. 

The application deadline is December 7, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

• 
be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

• 
join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

• 
help establish joint innovation projects in close collaboration with industry and the local society;

• 
help build up the research and educational environment;

• 
contribute to the teaching programmes in Software Engineering at the highest level for undergraduate and graduate students at SDU;

• 
join a harmonious workplace environment that is conducive to productivity, promotes creativity, and rewards and recognizes individuals and group achievement;

• 
have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

 

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Industrial Software is research and education in software engineering, embedded systems, cyber-security and AI engineering. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and embedded software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how new technologies change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

The positions are open in any of the AI engineering research areas of interest to the centres, which include:

• 
AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

• 
AI integration in mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

• 
Human-AI collaboration in the context of mobile, wearable and embedded platforms

• 
Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

 

Who we are looking for

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline. For associate professors we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated research excellence appropriate to their career stage, who show a clear path towards an independent and internationally recognised research programme, and who are able and willing to contribute to competitive national and international funding applications. We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

 

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense, Sønderborg and Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Sønderborg.

 

Curious?

If you are interested in learning more about the positions, please contact:

• 
Torben Worm (Head of Centres): tow@mmmi.sdu.dk

• 
Mikkel Baun Kjærgaard (Vice-Head of Centres): mbkj@mmmi.sdu.dk

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

 

Application procedure

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Cover letter.

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original and official English translation).

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Up to five most relevant publications to the position.

• 
A research statement.

• 
Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

• 
Up to three reference letters may be included (optional).

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included (optional).

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration no.) must be crossed out. All PDF files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected.

UPLOAD GUIDE: Cover letter shall be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae shall be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max. 5 MB). All other documents shall be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max. 10 files of max. 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is December 7, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an associate professor is permanent.

Employment as an associate professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level as well as scientific and teaching qualifications commensurate with the position as an associate professor. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for associate professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

• 
Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

The company

Our client is a venture-backed Copenhagen biotech that designs a new class of oral drugs. It uses its own generative AI, automated chemistry and high-throughput biology. The platform has made and tested hundreds of thousands of novel compounds, and the company has a major pharma partnership behind it. R&D is organised under a CTO across three groups: AI & Computational Drug Design, Platform Chemistry, and Screening Biology.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will own the company's internal scientific software, so every team works from the same clean, consistent data with tools that fit together.

The company creates, moves and decides on large volumes of chemistry and biology data. Today each team builds its own solutions. The company is moving to a new data platform built for its molecules and will build custom internal products on top of it.

The Product Manager is the person who sees that three teams are building three versions of the same thing and turns them into one that works for everyone. Success is measured in time saved for the scientists: the software should save more than it costs.

Responsibilities

Product ownership

• Owns the roadmap for the internal scientific software, starting with the three products above.

• Gathers and challenges requirements from computational design, chemistry and biology, and turns parallel requests into shared solutions.

• Prioritises with the leadership team: what gets built, in what order, and why.

• Makes sure the products connect to each other and to the data platform.

• Runs user testing and adoption with the scientists, and tracks the time saved.

Delivery and leadership

• Works agile, and knows where agility stops. Ships working products within months without painting the platform into a corner.

• Leads and coordinates 3–6 developers, a mix of contractors and hires. A front-end engineer may report directly.

• Helps shape the software team as it grows.

Hands-on, at the start

• Contributes to the build until the development team is in place. The stack is Python on the back end, React/Redux on the front end, and AWS serverless services.

• Judges which components fit together and which will break, including AI-assisted code.

The profile

The ideal candidate has experience from an environment where software is built and shipped, and a scientific background. Beyond that, in order of importance:

• People leadership. Has led developers or cross-functional teams, internal or contracted, and aligned stakeholders who don't report to them.

• Product management track record. Has owned a software product or platform from idea to adoption.

• Drug discovery experience. Has worked close to design, synthesis, screening or compound selection. Broader R&D software is also relevant.

• Scientific background. A chemistry or biology degree (either is fine). Knows what they don't know, and asks.

• Hands-on coding. Can build in Python and React. Judgement matters more than depth.

Mindset: curious enough to ask "what's a canonical SMILES?", pragmatic about agile, and happy to start hands-on and grow into leading a team.

Nice to have: AWS serverless, lab automation or screening data, ELN/LIMS or compound registration, startup or scale-up experience. The working language is English.

jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health at University of Copenhagen, Denmark, together with the The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomeds offers a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in causal inference with special focus on continuous-time causal inference, identification, and instrumental variables methods. 

  The anticipated hiring date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  About the Centre

  The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease.

  About the Section of Biostatistics
 The Section of Biostatistics carries out independent research in biostatistical applications and methods; it undertakes teaching of students at various educations, undergraduate as well as postgraduate, and it offers biostatistical advice to staff and students in all disciplines of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences. The section is internationally renowned for a high research level, especially within time-to-event analysis, while other competence areas include e.g. causal inference, latent variable modelling and prediction models. The section aims to maintain a strong position in these areas but also wants to expand into new areas of biostatistical research. The underlying idea is to produce high-level methodological research that is relevant in practical applications.

  More information on the Section of Biostatistics can be found at: https://biostat.ku.dk/. 
  

  Job Description
 We invite highly qualified, thorough, and motivated applicants to apply for a postdoctoral position in causal inference and statistical methodology. The successful candidate will conduct methodological research at the intersection of causal inference, event-history analysis, statistical machine learning, and semiparametric theory. Research will focus on the development of statistical methods for longitudinal and time-to-event data, with particular emphasis on continuously monitored data, dynamic treatment strategies, identification, and instrumental variable methods. Potential research directions include:  

   	
• causal inference for survival and competing risks outcomes 	
• continuous-time longitudinal causal models 	
• semiparametric and machine-learning-based estimation methods 	
• identification and estimation under instrumental variable assumptions 	
• methods for treatment switching, treatment discontinuation, and dynamic treatment interventions 	
• development of efficient and robust estimators for causal effects under complex longitudinal data structures   Example projects include the development of methods for causal inference with continuously observed treatment processes, incorporation of instrumental variables into survival analysis, and machine-learning-based estimation procedures for time-varying treatment effects. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute both theoretically and computationally, including development of new methodology, investigation of statistical properties, implementation of software, simulation studies, and applications to biomedical research questions. The candidate must participate in the interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment within the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed. The successful applicant is also encouraged to develop independent research directions aligned with the overall goals of the centre.

  The specific tasks of the position will include:

   	
• Manage own academic research and administrative activities. 	
• Conduct research in line with the goals of SMARTBiomed. 	
• Lead write-up of research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure, where appropriate, that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility. 	
• Present papers at conferences or public meetings. 	
• Contribute to the administrative activities of SMARTBiomed and the research group of appointment.   The postdoctoral fellow will also be encouraged and mentored to develop new proposals and research initiatives to support additional research. Over the course of the position, opportunities to teach at either the graduate or undergraduate level exist.

   

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:
 Essential experience and skills:

   	
• A Ph.D. in Statistics/Biostatistics, or similar disciplines.  	
• Strong skills in theoretical methods development.  	
• Experience and interest in data analysis and programming (e.g., in R) is further highly desirable.  	
• Strong English, scientific writing, and oral communications skills 	
• The ability to work independently, effectively, and collaboratively.    

  Terms of employment 
 The position is fixed term, limited to a period of 3 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 36,877.42 DKK/approx. 4,933.00 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Questions
 More information about the positions is available by contacting Associate Professor Helene Rytgaard, Section of Biostatistics, hely@sund.ku.dk, Professor Erin Gabriel, Section of Biostatistics, erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk, or Professor Torben Martinussen, Section of Biostatistics, tma@sund.ku.dk.   

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter indicating your motivation for application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications and archived works in progress.    

  Deadline for applications: December 1st, 2026.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery at the Department of Pharmacy

We are offering a PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery commencing 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  Our group and research

  Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have revolutionized the field of nucleic acid therapeutics and are now central to the development of mRNA-based medicines. Understanding the connection between nanoparticle composition, structure, and biological performance is essential for further advances in the field. The Vaccine Design and Delivery group investigates these relationships through a combination of biophysical, structural, and analytical approaches. The group also focuses on in vitro testing, in vivo imaging of biodistribution, and in vivo immunogenicity and protection studies in animal models. The overarching goal is to enable the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will join a new research program led by Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani, an expert in advanced physicochemical methods to study lipid self-assembly. 

  Project description

  The overall aim of the PhD project is to advance the understanding of lipid nanoparticle (LNP) systems for nucleic acid delivery through the integration of formulation design, structural characterization, and interaction studies. The candidate will employ state-of-the-art biophysical and structural techniques to investigate the nanoscale structure of LNPs and their behavior in biologically relevant environments. By combining advanced nanoparticle formulation with cutting-edge characterization methods, including scattering techniques and electron microscopy, the project seeks to establish quantitative relationships between LNP composition, structure, and biological interactions. These approaches will be used to investigate how LNP properties govern interactions with biological media and membranes, generating fundamental insights that will guide the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will work under the supervision of Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani within the Vaccine Design and Delivery group. The PhD fellowship is part of a larger research project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark through a Sapere Aude: DFF-Research Leader grant.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Camilla Foged, Department of Pharmacy, camilla.foged@sund.ku.dk, Direct Phone: +45 35 33 64 02.

  Start:            1 March 2027 (or after agreement)

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent research project under supervision.    	
• Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team. 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project 	
• Teaching and disseminating your knowledge. 	
• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme Description:

  The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., Physical chemistry, Biophysics, Nanotechnology or related fields).

  The successful candidate will specifically work on 1) formulation of mRNA-LNPs; 2) investigating the structure and morphology of LNPs in the absence and presence of biomimetic fluid; 3) understanding the mechanism of interaction of LNPs with model membranes.

  The project combines a range of experimental biophysical methods, including lab-based techniques and experiments at large-scale neutron and X-ray scattering facilities in Europe.

  Qualifications:
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  In connection with the appointment special importance will be attached to the applicant having the professional and personal qualifications stated below:

   

   	
• Obtained a Master´s degree in Physical chemistry, Biophysics, Nanotechnology, or related areas 	
• Excellent English speaking, reading and writing skills 	
• Creativity and ability to be both team-oriented and independent 	
• Capability of working at the interface between different disciplines 	
• Ability to thrive in an international research environment   Other important criteria are:

   	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Previous publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in physical and colloidal chemistry for nanomedicine applications 	
• Language skills 	
• Interest in travelling to large-scale synchrotron and neutron facilities to perform experiments   Preferred Qualifications 

  We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with an open-minded attitude towards quantitative analysis of the experimental data. The ideal candidate should also have a strong background and/or hands-on research experience within one or several of the fields mentioned below:

   	
• Lipid self-assembly and their biophysical characterization 	
• Small angle X-ray and neutron scattering (experiments and advanced data analysis)

Solid experience and an excellent track record gained in the field of lipid self-assembly and scattering will be considered a distinct advantage. We encourage all the qualified individuals - regardless of their personal background and status - to apply.

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment.

  The Dept. of Pharmacy offers a wide range of instrumentation (e.g., microfluidic mixing, cell labs). Core facilities at UCPH allow to access state-of-the-art equipment via a fee-for-service scheme (e.g., SAXS, cryoTEM). A substantial part of the work will rely on access to large scale facilities for neutron and x-rays scattering (national and international).

  Job Description
 The Perrier Lab at the Department of Neuroscience, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, is seeking a motivated and talented PhD fellow to study the impact of gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in GABAA  receptors implicated in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs).

  DEEs are severe early-onset conditions characterized by intractable epilepsy, intellectual disability, developmental delay or regression, movement disorders, and autism spectrum disorders. Although missense variants in GABAA receptor subunits are often assumed to cause loss of receptor function (LOF), recent work by our collaborators at the University of Sydney (Australia) and Filadelfia Hospital (Denmark) shows that GOF variants are just as prevalent, and their functional outcomes closely correlate with patient phenotypes.

  Project Overview
 The main goal of this project is to understand how mutations that increase inhibitory signaling in the brain can nevertheless lead to DEE. To address this, you will investigate animal models carrying GOF GABAA receptor mutations found in patients, examining their effects at multiple levels:

   	
• In Vivo  	 		
• Monitor animal behavior and record electrocorticographic (ECoG) activity to detect abnormalities linked to patient symptoms. 	 	 	
• In Vitro 	 		
• Use brain slice preparations to measure neuronal activity at the microcircuit level, comparing GOF mutants to wild-type littermates. This approach will clarify if microcircuits from the thalamocortical loop are impaired in GOF DEE models and if impairments are responsible for the epileptic phenotype. 	 	   Based on these findings, you will contribute to the design and testing of targeted treatments aimed at correcting the underlying defects, first in vitro and subsequently in vivo. This project will be conducted in close collaboration with Filadelfia Hospital, which maintains a cohort of patients affected by these rare and severe conditions.

Postdoctoral Fellow in Economic Analysis of Nature Restoration Measures Across Different Farming Systems

Are you interested in Economics of nature restoration in agriculture and can you contribute to the development of the Horizon Europe research project BALANCE? Then the Department of Environmental Science invites you to apply for a two-year Postdoc position. 

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two –year position from 1 May 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
• This section may include topics such as: 
• You will be contributing to/establishing/developing ... 
• You will be working primarily with ... 
• The position will focus on aspects of/elements of ... 
• You will be involved in ... 
• These activities will be in close collaboration with ...
The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to an interdisciplinary, EU-wide project investigating how nature restoration and nature-positive farming systems can contribute to biodiversity and farming. You will be working primarily with assessment of the short-, medium- and long-term costs and benefits of different nature restoration measures across different farming systems, with a focus on farm income, farm productivity and farm production. You will also develop methods for upscaling the findings on costs and benefits to the EU level. You will be involved in collaborations with researchers in agricultural and environmental economics as well as researchers in other disciplines and stakeholders collaborating in the same project.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in Environmental or Agricultural Economics or similar. Candidates should demonstrate strong skills in quantitative economics methods. Documented experience with farm economics and biodiversity is desirable.

We are looking for a candidate with:
• Strong analytical skills
• Experience in quantitative economic assessment related to agri-environmental challenges
• Experience in data collection from scientific articles and public and advisory reports 
• Demonstrated ability to publish scientific work in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English
• Ability to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:
• Experience in assessing environmental or agronomic topics across different spatial and time scales 
• Familiarity with policy-related research
• Experience in collaboration across disciplinary boundaries, particularly between natural and social sciences
We value motivated candidates with strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, who can engage constructively with researchers and stakeholders from different disciplinary and professional backgrounds. 

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technology at Aarhus University. The expertise ranges from economics, policy analysis, social science, and geography to physics, chemistry, microbiology and mathematical modelling. Both basic and applied research is conducted related to some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution, pollution control, land management, climate change, and energy systems, relevant to the quality of soil, water, air, biodiversity, and other ecosystem services. Advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders. Currently, about 170 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk/en/. The department is located at Risø Campus in Roskilde, 35 kilometers west of Copenhagen.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Environmental Social Science and Geography research unit. The unit employs approximately 25 staff, focusing on interdisciplinary analysis of the interlinkages between the environment and society from political science, economics and sociology perspectives. The strategic focus of the unit includes environmental policy development, regulation and instruments, understanding of actions and actors in policy formulation and implementation, spatially integrated modelling as well as policies and economics of ecosystem services and nature-based solutions. Research findings are used for dissemination to the research community, in advisory services to decision makers as well as for teaching.

Our ambition is to have an inclusive and open working environment. 

What we offer 
The department offers:

• an exciting interdisciplinary and international environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Katarina Elofsson, email katarina.elofsson@envs.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 10 January 2027 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

Section of Epidemiology - Perinatal, Obstetric & Pediatric Epidemiology (POPE) group
Department of Public Health
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

Do you have a strong methodological foundation and an interest in designing, analysing and interpreting epidemiological observational studies? Do you enjoy working with large-scale datasets from national registries and cohort studies to address important public health questions? And would you like to contribute to research with high societal relevance, focusing on health and development from early childhood to adulthood?

If so, we invite you to apply for a full-time position (37 hours/week) as Staff Scientist in the Perinatal, Obstetric & Paediatric Epidemiology (POPE) Group at the Section of Epidemiology, University of Copenhagen, starting 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. In this role, you will execute analytical tasks within epidemiological research projects using national registry and cohort data, while developing and maintaining research data resources.

About Section of Epidemiology and the POPE group 

The Section of Epidemiology conducts research on determinants of health and disease across the life-course, with the aim of improving public health and advancing epidemiological theory.

You will join the POPE group, whose research focuses on maternal, child, and adolescent health from a life-course perspective. Our work examines how perinatal and early childhood exposures influence health outcomes throughout childhood and into young adulthood. Research topics include preterm birth, infections and vaccinations during pregnancy, mental health, and psychiatric treatment. The POPE group extensively uses Danish registry data and the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC), which provides rich self-reported and biological data. DNBC is a nationwide birth cohort including more than 96,000 individuals born in 1996-2003 whose mothers enrolled during pregnancy – more details here. The group is deeply involved in ongoing and future DNBC data collections, long-term follow-up, and international cohort collaborations. For more details read here: POPE

About the Department
The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

About the Position
The Staff Scientist will play a central role in advancing and executing epidemiological research within the POPE group. Working collaboratively with researchers, external collaborators, and colleagues across the Department of Public Health, with opportunities of conducting independent research, while the primary responsibility is to contribute and execute projects led by others based on large-scale Danish registry and cohort data. Responsibilities will include developing and maintaining research data resources, ensuring rigorous data quality, performing advanced analytical and statistical workflows, and contributing to the establishment/maintenance of data infrastructures that enable high-quality epidemiological research and peer-reviewed publications. The tasks include:

• 
Developing, maintaining, and quality assuring large-scale epidemiological data resources based on Danish national registries and cohort data including the DNBC.

• 
Contributing to the design, implementation, and conduct of epidemiological research projects by preparing analytical datasets, performing descriptive and statistical analyses, and supporting the interpretation and dissemination of findings.

• 
Coordinating key research activities related to the DNBC, including the ongoing 25-year follow-up and international federated analyses across cohorts.

• 
Establishing data set-ups where cohort data are embedded within register-based populations for resources beyond DNBC

• 
Providing methodological and analytical support to a broad range of epidemiological research projects within the group, contributing expertise in study implementation, data handling, troubleshooting and project development as needed.

• 
Taking responsibility for data security, exportation of analysis results, data governance and GDPR compliance within the POPE group

Profile and Qualifications

• 
Preferably a PhD in epidemiology and/or, public health or related fields.

• 
Advanced methodological and analytical skills, including demonstrated experience with data management, study design, statistical modelling, and interpretation of observational epidemiological data.

• 
A proven ability to envision, plan, and execute epidemiological research projects independently, while delivering work to agreed deadlines.

• 
Proven experience working with large and complex datasets from Danish national registries, large cohorts, or other longitudinal data sources using R, STATA and/or SAS.

• 
Strong scientific writing skills, with a track record of preparing and publishing peer-reviewed publications and project documentation.

• 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide expert methodological guidance and explain complex findings to researchers from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative fashion.

• 
Fluency in Danish (both written and spoken) is required, as the role involves working extensively with Danish national registry data and documentation.

• 
Experience in, or a strong interest in perinatal and life-course epidemiology, including research on child development, adolescent health, and/or mental health.

Place of employment
The place of employment is Section of Epidemiology, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen located near the city lakes in Central Copenhagen.

Terms of employment
The position is a full-time position (37 working hours weekly).
The starting date is 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on seniority with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experiences and qualifications.

Questions
For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor and Research group leader Katrine Strandberg-Larsen, email: ksla@sund.ku.dk. For questions regarding the recruitment procedure, please contact HR at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences: HR-IFSV@adm.ku.dk

Application

Curriculum Vitae, including education, work/research experience, language skills, and any other skills relevant to the position.

A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education.
